arguments.content:
---
name: slack-api
description: "Interact with the Slack Web API: send, update, and delete messages, reply in threads, read channel/DM history and conversations, list users, add reactions, search messages, upload files, and compose rich Block Kit messages. Use when the user asks to post to Slack, read Slack channels or DMs, build a Slack bot or integration, resolve Slack tokens or scopes, or format Slack messages."
---

# Slack API

Automate a Slack workspace through the Slack Web API. Cover messaging, threads, conversations, users, reactions, search, file uploads, and Block Kit formatting.

## Before you start

1. Require an access token: a bot token (`xoxb-...`) or user token (`xoxp-...`) from a Slack app installed in the target workspace.
2. Read the token from the `SLACK_TOKEN` environment variable. Never hard-code a token or print it. If `SLACK_TOKEN` is unset, stop and ask the user to set it (e.g. `export SLACK_TOKEN=xoxb-...`).
3. If a call fails with a scope error, ask the user to add the missing scope in the Slack app config and reinstall the app.

## Make an API call

Prefer the bundled helper script — it handles auth, errors, and truncates output to protect the context window:

```bash
node scripts/slack_request.mjs chat.postMessage '{"channel":"general","text":"Hello from a bot"}'
```

Equivalent raw call when the helper is unusable:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \
  -d '{"channel":"general","text":"Hello from a bot"}'
```

Every response is JSON with a top-level `ok` boolean. On failure, report the `error` value plus the `needed`/`provided` scopes to the user.

## Common workflows

- **Send a message or thread reply** → `chat.postMessage`. Reply in a thread by passing the parent message `ts` as `thread_ts`. Pass a list of channels to the bot must join first (`conversations.join`) or include `chat:write.public`.
- **List channels and read history** → `conversations.list`, `conversations.history`, `conversations.replies`.
- **Read users** → `users.list`, `users.info`, `users.lookupByEmail`.
- **React to a message** → `reactions.add` with the message `ts`.
- **Edit or delete messages your bot posted** → `chat.update`, `chat.delete`.
- **Search** → `search.messages`.

Use channel IDs (e.g. `C123...`) in code paths; channel names like `general` also work for most messaging methods.

## Message formatting

- Plain, single-line text: use the `text` field.
- Rich layouts (headers, fields, buttons, images, context): compose **Block Kit** JSON — read `references/block-kit.md`.
- Keep plain messages under 40,000 chars and Block Kit `text` fields under 3,000 chars.

## Reference material

- `references/methods.md` — method/scope tables, pagination, rate limits, common errors. Read when choosing an API method or diagnosing a failure.
- `references/block-kit.md` — Block Kit layout cheat sheet with copy-paste payloads. Read when building rich messages.

## Output discipline

- Summarize results in 2–5 lines (message `ts`, channel, item counts, permalink). Do not dump full raw JSON to the user.
- When listing many items (users, messages, channels), show the first ~10 and mention the total count plus pagination status.

# Slack Web API Method Reference

## Table of contents

- [Calling conventions](#calling-conventions)
- [Identifiers and timestamps](#identifiers-and-timestamps)
- [Messaging methods](#messaging-methods)
- [Conversation methods](#conversation-methods)
- [User methods](#user-methods)
- [Reaction methods](#reaction-methods)
- [Search and files](#search-and-files)
- [Pagination](#pagination)
- [Rate limits](#rate-limits)
- [Common errors](#common-errors)

## Calling conventions

- Base URL: `https://slack.com/api/<method>`; method names are `snake_case` (e.g. `chat.postMessage`).
- Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; send JSON bodies with `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`.
- Every response is JSON: `{"ok": true, ...}` on success or `{"ok": false, "error": "<name>", "needed": "...", "provided": "..."}` on failure.
- Bot tokens start `xoxb-`, user tokens `xoxp-`. Bot tokens act as the app's bot user and are subject to "bot must be in the channel" rules.
- Token lives in the `SLACK_TOKEN` environment variable. Never hard-code or echo tokens.

## Identifiers and timestamps

- Channel IDs start `C`, user IDs `U`, team IDs `T`, file IDs `F`.
- Message timestamps (`ts`) look like `"1234567890.123456"` — seconds since the Unix epoch with microseconds. Treat them as opaque strings; never parse/format them as dates client-side.
- Channel names (e.g. `general`) are accepted by most messaging methods for public channels, but IDs are reliable everywhere.
- Resolve name → ID with `conversations.list` (match `name` + `is_channel`/`is_private`) or `users.lookupByEmail`.
- `chat.postMessage` returns `ts` and `channel`; use the returned `ts` as `thread_ts` to reply in that thread.

## Messaging methods

| Method | Key parameters | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chat.postMessage` | `channel`*, `text` and/or `blocks`, `thread_ts`, `reply_broadcast`, `mrkdwn`, `link_names`, `unfurl_links` | `chat:write` (+ `chat:write.public` to post to public channels without joining) | Returns `ts`, `channel`, `message`. Max 40,000 chars total. |
| `chat.update` | `channel`*, `ts`*, `text` and/or `blocks` | `chat:write` | Can only update messages posted by the same app/user token. |
| `chat.delete` | `channel`*, `ts`* | `chat:write` | Can only delete messages posted by the same app/user token. |
| `chat.postEphemeral` | `channel`*, `user`*, `text`/`blocks` | `chat:write` | Message visible only to the target `user`. |
| `chat.getPermalink` | `channel`*, `message_ts`* | none required | Returns `permalink` for sharing. |

`*` = required.

## Conversation methods

| Method | Key parameters | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `conversations.list` | `types` (e.g. `public_channel,private_channel,im,mpim`), `exclude_archived`, `limit`, `cursor` | `channels:read`, `groups:read`, `im:read`, `mpim:read` | Paginated; use `cursor`. |
| `conversations.info` | `channel`* | matching read scope | Returns conversation metadata. |
| `conversations.history` | `channel`*, `limit`, `cursor`, `oldest`, `latest`, `inclusive` | `channels:history`, `groups:history`, `im:history`, `mpim:history` | Messages newest-first. Bots only see history of channels they are in. |
| `conversations.replies` | `channel`*, `ts`* | history scopes above | Fetch a thread: pass the parent message `ts`. |
| `conversations.members` | `channel`* | read scopes above | Paginated member list. |
| `conversations.open` | `channel` or `users` | `im:write` (DMs), `groups:write` (MPIMs), `channels:manage` | Opens or returns an existing DM/MPIM/conversation. |
| `conversations.join` | `channel`* | `channels:write` or `groups:write` | Make the bot join a channel; public channels only. |

`*` = required.

Bots can only see/read channels they belong to. To read a public channel the bot is not in: `conversations.join` first (needs `channels:write`), or post once with `chat:write.public`.

## User methods

| Method | Key parameters | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `users.list` | `limit`, `cursor`, `include_locale` | `users:read` | Paginated; large workspaces need cursor looping. |
| `users.info` | `user`* | `users:read` | Profile incl. real name, display name, email if authorized. |
| `users.lookupByEmail` | `email`* | `users:read.email` | Best way to map an email to a user ID. |

`*` = required.

## Reaction methods

| Method | Key parameters | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reactions.add` | `channel`*, `name`* (no colons), `timestamp`* | `reactions:write` | Fails with `already_reacted` if the user already reacted. |
| `reactions.remove` | `channel`*, `name`*, `timestamp`* | `reactions:write` | |
| `reactions.get` | `channel`*, `timestamp`* | `reactions:read` | Returns `message.reactions[]` with `name` and `count`. |

`*` = required.

## Search and files

| Method | Key parameters | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `search.messages` | `query`* | `search:read` | Query syntax: `from:@alice in:#general after:2024-01-01`. |
| `files.upload` | `channels`, `filename`, `content` or `file` | `files:write` | Modern version accepts JSON with `content` (text) or `external_id`. For binary uploads use multipart: `curl -F file=@./report.pdf -F channels=general -F "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN" https://slack.com/api/files.upload`. |
| `files.info` | `file`* | `files:read` | Metadata + download URL. |

`*` = required.

## Pagination

- List-style methods return `response_metadata.next_cursor` when more results exist.
- Loop: call again with `"cursor": "<next_cursor>"` until `next_cursor` is empty or you have enough items.
- Do not loop forever: cap total pages (e.g. 20) and report to the user when the cap is hit.
- `conversations.history` + `conversations.replies` are the sanctioned way to page through message history.

## Rate limits

- Slack applies per-method **tiers** (Tier 1–4) per app+workspace+token combination; Tier 1 is most lenient, Tier 4 strictest (e.g. `search.messages`).
- On HTTP `429`, read the `Retry-After` header (seconds) and wait before retrying; use exponential backoff with jitter for repeated calls.
- Never poll in tight loops. Batch reads with `limit` and pause between pages.
- Treat `internal_error`/`fatal_error` as transient; retry with backoff up to ~3 times, then report failure.

## Common errors

| `error` value | Meaning / action |
|---|---|
| `invalid_auth` | Token is bad or revoked. Ask the user for a valid token. |
| `account_inactive` | Associated Slack account is disabled. |
| `missing_scope` | Token lacks permission; response includes `needed` (add it in app config and reinstall) and `provided`. |
| `not_in_channel` | Bot must join the channel first (`conversations.join`) or be invited. |
| `channel_not_found` | Wrong ID/name, or the bot can't see the conversation. Verify with `conversations.info`. |
| `is_archived` | Channel is archived; unarchive in Slack UI. |
| `msg_too_long` | Exceeded 40,000 chars; shorten or use blocks. |
| `invalid_blocks` | Block Kit JSON invalid; re-validate against `references/block-kit.md`. |
| `restricted_action` | Enterprise/org policy blocks it; inform the user. |
| `already_reacted` | Reaction already exists for this user. |
| `rate_limited` | HTTP 429 — honor `Retry-After`. |
| `internal_error` | Transient; retry with backoff. |

Diagnosis routine: on `ok:false`, read `error`, then `needed`/`provided`, then explain the fix in plain language (add scope + reinstall, join channel, fix payload, retry after N seconds).

# Block Kit Reference

## Table of contents

- [Rules and limits](#rules-and-limits)
- [Block types](#block-types)
- [Plain text vs mrkdwn](#plain-text-vs-mrkdwn)
- [Copy-paste payloads](#copy-paste-payloads)
- [Validation checklist](#validation-checklist)

Block Kit is Slack's structured JSON format for message layouts. Send it in the `blocks` field of `chat.postMessage` (optionally with a plain-text `text` fallback for notifications).

## Rules and limits

- Max **50 blocks** per message.
- Max 3,000 chars per `text` field inside a block; max 75 chars per heading (`header`) text.
- `section.fields[]` accepts 2–10 items (use even counts for nice grid layout).
- `mrkdwn` text renders Slack formatting (`*bold*`, `_italic_`, `~strike~`, `` `code` ``, links `<https://...|label>`, mentions `<@U123>`); `plain_text` renders literally.
- One `actions` block can hold up to 5 elements (buttons, selects, etc.).
- Interactive elements (buttons, selects, datepicker) require the message to be posted with `chat.postMessage` from an app — they work in bot messages without extra setup.
- Always provide `text` (fallback) alongside `blocks` for accessibility and notifications.
- Do not mix top-level `attachments` (legacy) with `blocks` in new code.

## Block types

| Block | `type` | Purpose | Key fields |
|---|---|---|---|
| Section | `section` | Main content: text and/or fields | `text` (mrkdwn/plain_text), `fields[]`, `accessory` (button/image/overflow) |
| Header | `header` | Large heading, up to 75 chars | `text` (plain_text only, max 150 chars total w/ emoji) |
| Divider | `divider` | Horizontal rule | none |
| Context | `context` | Small secondary text (up to 10 elements, 25 chars avg per plain item) | `elements[]` |
| Image | `image` | Image with alt text | `image_url`, `alt_text`, optional `title` |
| Actions | `actions` | Interactive buttons/selects | `elements[]` |
| Input | `input` | Interactive form field (modal-only in most cases; not for messages) | `label`, `element`, `block_id` |
| File | `file` | Embedded file (message only) | `external_id`, `source: "remote"` |

## Plain text vs mrkdwn

```json
{"type": "section", "text": {"type": "plain_text", "text": "Literal *not bold*"}}
{"type": "section", "text": {"type": "mrkdwn", "text": "Bold *deploy finished* and <https://example.com|view logs>"}}
```

- `header`, `input.label`, and button labels require `plain_text`.
- `section.text`, `context` elements, and option labels accept `mrkdwn`.

## Copy-paste payloads

### 1. Simple formatted message

```json
{
  "channel": "general",
  "text": "Deploy finished",
  "blocks": [
    {"type": "header", "text": {"type": "plain_text", "text": "🚀 Deploy finished"}},
    {"type": "section", "text": {"type": "mrkdwn", "text": "Version *2.4.1* is live in <https://example.com|production>."}},
    {"type": "divider"},
    {"type": "context", "elements": [{"type": "mrkdwn", "text": "Triggered by <@U123456> • 42s"}]}
  ]
}
```

### 2. Section with fields (metrics)

```json
{
  "channel": "general",
  "blocks": [
    {"type": "section", "text": {"type": "mrkdwn", "text": "Daily report"}},
    {"type": "section", "fields": [
      {"type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*Users:*\n1,204"},
      {"type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*Errors:*\n3"},
      {"type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*P95 latency:*\n182 ms"},
      {"type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*Uptime:*\n99.98%"}
    ]}
  ]
}
```

### 3. Message with a button

```json
{
  "channel": "general",
  "text": "Approve the release?",
  "blocks": [
    {"type": "section", "text": {"type": "mrkdwn", "text": "Approve release *2.4.1* to production?"}, "accessory": {"type": "button", "text": {"type": "plain_text", "text": "Approve"}, "style": "primary", "value": "approve_2_4_1"}},
    {"type": "actions", "elements": [{"type": "button", "text": {"type": "plain_text", "text": "Roll back"}, "style": "danger", "value": "rollback_2_4_1"}]}
  ]
}
```

### 4. Thread reply with an image

```json
{
  "channel": "general",
  "thread_ts": "1234567890.123456",
  "text": "Screenshot attached",
  "blocks": [
    {"type": "section", "text": {"type": "mrkdwn", "text": "Here is the failing UI:"}},
    {"type": "image", "image_url": "https://example.com/screenshot.png", "alt_text": "Screenshot of failing UI"}
  ]
}
```

## Validation checklist

1. Every block has a valid `type` and required fields; JSON parses (`invalid_blocks` error otherwise).
2. All plain-text fields that require `plain_text` use it (headers, button labels, inputs).
3. No block exceeds 3,000 chars; ≤ 50 blocks; `header` ≤ 75 chars.
4. A `text` fallback is always included at the message top level.
5. `block_id`/`action_id` values are unique when you need to handle interactions later.
